fields.v: Iscan, M. (2026). Learning When to Remember: Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandits for Abstention-Aware Memory Retrieval in LLM-Based Coding Agents. arXiv:2604.27283v1 [cs.CL], 30 Apr 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2604.27283v1; Springer-style template; text mentions future 'final journal claims', no published venue stated
PythaLab, Yildiz Technical University, Istanbul, Türkiye (single author)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — RSCB-MC, a risk-sensitive contextual-bandit memory controller for coding agents, evaluated against retrieval and bandit baselines on deterministic smoke-scale proxy benchmarks
fields.why: Judgement: RSCB-MC is compared with nine retrieval and bandit baselines and an oracle on the same artifacts (Tables 4-9), so 'secondary: Compares' fits at least as well as 'Evaluates'; the main nature (Proposes an approach) is clear
fields.doubt: O RSCB-MC é comparado com nove baselines nos mesmos artefactos. Decide se a natureza secundária é 'Evaluates' ou 'Compares'; a principal ('Proposes an approach') não levanta dúvidas.

fields.v: RSCB-MC (Risk-Sensitive Contextual Bandit with Memory Control), implemented in the pythalab-codex-issue-memory artifact (commit 227bbe3, Python 3.12.3); no release version

Pattern-variant-episode issue-memory records (canonical root-cause pattern, context-specific variants with command/path/stack signatures, validated episodes); fixed 16-feature state vector (Table 1); action set of 7 actions (no memory, top1 resolution, top3 summary, high-precision retrieval, high-recall retrieval, abstain, ask feedback); risk-sensitive reward (false-positive penalty γ=4.0 > verified α=2.0 > accepted β=1.0). No specification document

Normalize debugging context to query profile; retrieve candidate memories; build 16-feature state; score each action (Eq. 17); safety override (replace unsafe injection by abstain/no memory); apply action; observe feedback; compute reward; update policy (Algorithm 1)
Not stated as review points; 'ask feedback' action requests clarification or external feedback before reuse (in the evaluation, feedback comes from replay metadata)
Memory controller only, evaluated offline on deterministic replay/proxy artifacts; no LLM or coding agent run
Not classifiable (agent memory-gating method, no specification); author does not use SDD terms
Not applicable in the evaluation (memory decisions for debugging; motivating setting: debugging an existing Python repository)

Smoke scale: 24 canonical retrieval queries, 96 paraphrases, 32 hard-negative cases, 40 replay events per seed (2 seeds), 16 memory records, 32 variants, 24 context-budget cases, 56 abstention cases, 200-case hot-path validation per method (full target scale exists but not reported)
Local Python development/debugging failures (SQLite locking, stale migrations, wrong virtual environment, PYTHONPATH, configuration keys, etc.)

Configurations are memory-control methods; no agent or model run. Success metric: accepted/verified reuse or safe abstention per replay/proxy labels; the author states no success criterion (threshold), so for every entry below the quality verdict and the cost verdict are 'no criterion stated by the authors'. fields.why: r1 verdicts (works / partly / does not work) were judged 'on proxy data alone' with cut-offs the paper does not give; the author states no success criterion, so all verdicts replaced by 'no criterion stated by the authors' (rule of 2026-11-23). Added the full-retriever configuration and paraphrase R@1 (Table 4) and the missing hard-negative values (Table 5)

fields.v: Tasks: seeded smoke-scale artifacts (queries, paraphrases, hard negatives, replay events). Configurations: retrieval baselines (lexical, static hybrid, static hybrid + abstention, full retriever) and bandit baselines (epsilon-greedy, UCB1, Thompson, LinUCB, risk-sensitive Thompson) vs RSCB-MC, oracle upper bound. Held constant: same artifacts and seeds, deterministic scripts. Acceptance criterion: proxy labels from replay metadata. Repetitions: 2 deterministic seeds. Human intervention: none

RSCB-MC best non-oracle replay success (62.5% vs 60.0% risk-sensitive TS, 50.0% static) with 0.0% FP (static 17.5%); 5 points below oracle; 0% FP on hard negatives vs 75% static hybrid; sub-millisecond p95 latency. No significance tests

Distinguished methods on FP and proxy success; canonical retrieval saturated (all 100%), so it did not distinguish retrieval methods. Deterministic, so repeatable. Limitations stated: smoke scale, offline replay not causal, proxy labels, reward magnitude may not alter action selection

Smoke-scale evidence only; offline replay is not a causal online evaluation; hot-path labels are proxies; context-budget and dry-run experiments are proxy tasks; single-step bandit does not model delayed multi-turn effects or memory aging; controller over-conservative (wrong abstentions); inherits stale/contradictory memory. Future: full-scale benchmark, live LLM-agent evaluation, calibration, off-policy evaluation, long-horizon modeling

Abstract and conclusion highlight 62.5% / 0.0% FP; the 'agent dry-run' experiment mentioned in limitations (p. 22) is not reported in results. Abstention text (p. 15) says RSCB-MC 'answers 0.0% of cases' and p. 19 says it 'refuses all cases', yet Table 7 gives correct abstention 5.0%; different benchmarks, not reconciled. Tables partly jumbled by pdftotext; values read in column order. No LLM or coding agent used in any experiment. Code and artifacts at github.com/PhiniteLab/codex-issue-memory. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
Yes (1): problem and contributions clearly stated; no formal RQs
Yes (1): method formalised (features, actions, reward coefficients, algorithm), commit and seed given, code released
Partly (0.5): artifact commit and Python version given; no agent or model involved, so the agent claim is not tested
fields.why: No agent or model is used at all; the only tool (the artifact) is identified by commit and Python version. Whether that is Partly, Yes (everything used is identified) or No (the coding-agent claim is never tied to an agent or model) is a judgement
fields.doubt: Nenhum agente nem modelo foi usado; só o artefacto (commit 227bbe3, Python 3.12.3) está versionado. Decide se isto vale Partly, Yes ou No.

fields.v: Yes (1): artifact sizes and failure families described (Table 3) and the artifacts released; they are synthetic smoke-scale proxy data, which bears on Q5/Q9 rather than availability
fields.why: Q4 asks whether tasks are described and available; both hold (Table 3, GitHub), and the proxy nature bears on Q5/Q9. But individual cases are described only by family and count, so Partly is also defensible
fields.doubt: Os casos são descritos só por família e contagem (Tabela 3), mas os artefactos estão publicados no GitHub. Decide entre Yes e Partly.

fields.v: No (0): success and FP judged by author-built replay/proxy labels, no independent criterion
Yes (1): proxy quality, safety, token and latency metrics defined
Yes (1): several retrieval and bandit baselines and an oracle on the same artifacts
No (0): deterministic, 2 seeds, no variance or statistical analysis
fields.why: Two deterministic seeds are a limited form of repetition, so Partly is defensible; but per-seed results, variance and statistical tests are not reported, which supports No
fields.doubt: Há dois seeds determinísticos, mas os resultados por seed e a variância não são reportados. Decide entre No e Partly.

fields.v: Partly (0.5): claims explicitly scoped to proxy evidence, but framed as relevant to coding agents without any agent evaluation; abstention inconsistency
fields.why: Judgement: the 'Where this evidence stops' section scopes the claims carefully, so a reader could give Yes; the title and practical implications for coding agents rest on no agent run, and the abstention figures are not reconciled
fields.doubt: A secção 'Where this evidence stops' delimita bem as conclusões, mas o título e as implicações falam de agentes sem nenhum agente testado. Decide entre Partly e Yes.
